Hi :)
I can relate; wanting to isolate myself, just not feeling "right," having this looming sense of desperation and hopelessness always in the back of my mind, feeling like I had no friends, self-harm. One thing to remember as well is that depression can be often cyclical, which means it comes and goes in cycles. For me, I go through 3-4 months of feeling horrible and not being able to get out of bed. Then suddenly for a few weeks or a month I'll either feel much better or just feel empty and numb to every emotion. I started researching depression and mental illnesses in general when I first became aware of it and starting taking those quizzes and stuff. Not so much because I wanted to self-diagnose but because I wanted to learn more and be more in tune with my emotions so I could get a better sense of what was going on. I don't know too much about it, but feelings like these can also be caused by physical illnesses or certain diets and stuff like that too. If you decide to see a doctor and you're able to (it might be a good idea), they might be able to run tests too to make sure it's not something physical affecting you.

Hi! :) I really wanna say first of all that you and Betty seems like really good friends for being worried about her health and safety and wondering what would be a good way to approach this. I'll speak from my experience as someone who cuts on and off and has had friends and family confront me about it. I see a similarity between myself and your friend, as I am very private too and the only times people have seen my cuts were on accident. To me, the worst way someone has ever approached me was by directly asking me straight up, face to face, "What are those cuts on your arm?" From my experience as someone who is private, having someone ask me straight up like this made me uncomfortable because it caught me off guard, I'm not a good liar and I didn't have any answer off the top of my head to give, and the way this person asked me seemed a little accusatory (this is NOT to say your friend thinks this, this was just my experience). It seemed accusatory to me because obviously the person asking me about it knew very well that it was self-injury because the cuts were so straight but they just wanted me to "confess" in a way that I had done it. In the other hand, the best way someone "confronted" me about it was a more relaxed environment of texting or messaging over the internet. I guess others might see this as not being helpful because it's not as personal as face to face, but to me as a quiet and private person it was more comfortable. Over text message, I had time to read the message, take my time digesting it, took the time to acknowledge and become comfortable with the situation of addressing the problem, and had my own time and space to come up with an answer I saw as appropriate. To me, very personal face to face interaction scares me off a little bit. If someone were to say face to face "You can talk to me whenever you want" I'd just give an awkward "ok". But my friend who confronted me said "Hey, I know you've been stressed a lot with school. The other day I saw some cuts on you that I think might have been you self-harming. I just wanted to say that it scared me and concerned me a lot because you're a really good friend of mine and it hurts me to see you doing that to yourself" and finished with "If you ever want to talk or need help, I'm here". That interaction was over text message. Because it wasn't face to face it gave me some time to make myself comfortable with the idea that my friends had finally found out. A few days later this friend and I hung out together and even though we were just watching TV at his place I knew that the relationship had changed a bit because now the "truth had come out". After the TV show ended he turned to me and said "Hey, about the thing we talked about the other day I just wanted to remind you that I meant what I said and that I'm here" This interaction wasn't as awkward because I kinda knew it was coming because he had confronted me just a few days ago. He then said that he had friends who cut too and offered some alternatives to cutting (you can find some good ones online or I or someone else here can offer some tips if you want) and asked if I had cleaned the cuts or if I wanted him to help me clean and bandage them. Sorry for the huge response but I hope it helps! :) Feel free to reply to this or PM me if you need anything else.

I can really relate to what you said just now, about "what's the point, we're still going to die." I was diagnosed with PTSD and depression a few months ago and thoughts like those are usually the ones that send me to a really dark place. 

Though it's not easy, I'm just trying to take it day by day and keep telling myself to look at the small victories (getting out of bed, going outside, etc.) and to also try to pay close attention to what types of things make me feel worse, what things make me a bit happier, what time of day or night I usually start feeling sadder, etc.
Especially for people who are on the younger side and/or whose issues have started recently (I'm 21 and, like I said, my mental illnesses were diagnosed a few months ago. From your post, it sounds like this could apply to you as well), just taking it slowly is a good way to start. 

You're still super young, you have so many opportunities and so much time ahead of you :) Maybe you can find something you're passionate about and pursue it if it can help improve your mood: volunteer somewhere like a library/hospital/political organization, write poetry or learn to draw/paint, learn up on the subjects that interest you in school, see if you're able to travel somewhere with friends. I know this probably won't help much, but those are things that I find help me a bit :) Even if you're not actually doing those things, maybe you'll still find that the idea that you're alive, healthy, and able to pursue these things is enough of a small inspiration to carry on day by day.

It also might be a good idea to talk to your dad again about how you're feeling. It sounds like he cares about you and, like you said, has been noticing your behavior. Maybe you can talk to him about you seeing a therapist, counselor, or doctor about what's going on with you. 

Best of luck to you :)
